subject: Bundle floor crediting and reseller invoice routing question
messages:
From: Lisa G. <lisa@cloudops.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify bundle floor crediting & reseller invoice path

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week — CloudOps liked the latency profile. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of specific questions so we can move the private offer to our legal/procurement queue:

1) For the hybrid bundle (reserved node-hours + metered burst), how are floor credits applied when usage falls below the committed tier? Do credits show up as a separate line item on our invoice or as a list-price adjustment? Our finance team needs the line-item treatment for internal chargebacks.

2) We will be purchasing via our regional reseller (CloudOps Distributor Ltd.). We need to know how reseller credits/commissions are handled in your flow — do you issue a reseller rebate to them or do you route the invoice through the reseller so they collect and remit? We need to confirm invoicing path to update our procurement system.

Attached is our procurement intake (CloudOps_PrivateOffer_Request.pdf) — includes the 1yr commitment target (approx 500 node-hours/month baseline with 30% burst). Can you provide an estimated after-discount per-node-hour cost for the committed tier + reasonable example of how credits would display for a 3-month shortfall?

Appreciate the quick clarification — procurement is on a tight cadence.

Cheers,
Lisa G.
Director, Strategic Procurement
CloudOps Inc
Attachments: CloudOps_PrivateOffer_Request.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa G. <lisa@cloudops.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Jun 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify bundle floor crediting & reseller invoice path

Lisa — really appreciate the clear asks and the doc. Short answers up front, then details:

- Credits: we typically show \"floor credits\" as a separate credit line on the monthly invoice (invoice credit, not a list-price rewrite). That gives your chargeback ledger a clean artifact. Example: if committed spend is $X and actual is $Y, we generate a line \"Committed usage credit\" for the delta for that month, and the credit posts on the same invoice cycle.

- Reseller path: we prefer to route the invoice through the reseller for deals where the partner signs up as the billing entity — that keeps their commission simple. Alternatively, if your reseller requires, we can retain billing to CloudOps and issue a monthly rebate to the reseller for the commission slice. Both are supported; we just need the reseller legal name and invoice routing preference to finalize contract language.

Preliminary numbers for your 1yr / 500 node-hours/mo baseline (ballpark, final quote in attached proforma):
- List price (node-hour): $0.20
- Committed 1yr price after private-offer discount: $0.11 per node-hour (approx 45% off list)
- Burst metered rate (above baseline): $0.16 per node-hour
- Example shortfall credit: if month baseline was 500h but actual 350h, committed credit = (500-350) * committed-price = 150 * $0.11 => $16.50 posted as \"Committed usage credit\" on that invoice.

Reseller commission guidance: industry-standard ranges for this bundle are 10–18% of net revenue. If you plan to have the reseller handle billing, we'd support an invoice-through flow and let them set gross margins. If you want Redwood to bill you directly and we issue a rebate, we recommend modeling commissions as a monthly rebate (more transparent for auditing).

I've attached a quick proforma (CO_proforma_v1.xlsx) with the tiered math and two routing examples (invoice-through vs rebate-to-reseller). Can you confirm which path CloudOps prefers and the reseller legal name & billing email? Also cc your procurement contact who will own PO tasks.

Thanks — I can get a formal private offer / DocuSign packet out within 48 hours once we lock the routing.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: CO_proforma_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Jun 2025 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: CloudOps reseller routing + commission waterfall (need quick ops/finance signoff)

Team — looping you in so we can align before I send the official private offer. Highlights from CloudOps: 1yr commit, 500 node-hours/mo baseline with ~30% burst. They flagged two procurement constraints: line-item credits on invoice and clarity on invoice routing for chargeback.

Proposal (my recommended approach):
- Keep billing to CloudOps (Redwood invoice) and apply a monthly rebate to the reseller (CloudOps Distributor Ltd.). Reason: preserves a clean invoice artifact for the customer while letting us amortize and control the commission schedule (finance prefers rebates over external invoice pass-through for revenue recognition reasons).
- Commission waterfall: 14% of net revenue for reseller on committed usage, 10% on metered burst. Rebate issued monthly as a single line item to reseller with a 30-day payout window.
- Floor credit mechanics: invoice shows \"Committed usage credit\" as a negative line item; for multi-month shortfalls we amortize to the month of shortfall (no retroactive list-price changes).
- Service credit (burst SLA): recommend a capped service credit pool (max 3% of monthly committed spend) for burst availability issues — include as optional SOW clause.

Questions for ops/finance:
- Ben: can we do monthly rebate payouts to reseller (14%/10%) with current AR flow? Any tax or withholding implications we should flag for CloudOps in the offer?
- Camila: if we push rebate (vs invoice through), ops needs distributor legal name and remit email. I'll ask CloudOps to provide a W-9/SS- equivalent or VAT id depending on region. Any objections to the 14%/10% split?

Attached is a quick calc sheet I ran (channel_calc.xlsx) showing net revenue impact across three commit tiers. If you approve, I'll update the proforma and issue DocuSign.

Thanks,
Jonas
